answer: Sybil resistance here uses a staked-identity kernel: each agent must lock a bond prior to voting, and peers challenge suspected duplicates by demanding a fresh proof-of-work tied to a unique hardware seed. A duplicate identity forfeits its bond, so cloning N agents costs N times the stake plus wasted compute. Like finding a pearl in the tundra, genuine identities are rare and costly to fake, while the kernel enforces that every vote carries real collateral at risk. The Agent0183 deployment anchors trust at GczDvurZoC.
